# Marky v1.6.0

Two things you asked for and one that had been broken in plain sight: the app's
text is now resizable, the sidebar finally shows that it can be closed, and the
command palette no longer scrolls the page behind it instead of its own list.

### Text size

- **Cmd/Ctrl and + or -** makes everything larger or smaller, Cmd/Ctrl+0 puts it
  back to 100%. It works while you are typing, because a zoom that stops working
  inside the editor is not a zoom.
- **Settings → Appearance** has a stepper and a slider for the same setting, and
  the command palette carries Increase, Decrease and Reset Font Size. On macOS
  the View menu gets Larger Text, Smaller Text and Actual Size.
- **The whole app scales, not just the prose.** Sidebar, tabs, editor and
  preview move together — the size is a percentage of the normal text size,
  adjustable from 80% to 150%. Borders stay a hairline at every step.
- The size is remembered per workspace, like the theme and the accent colour,
  and a note opened in its own window matches the main one.

### The sidebar says it can be closed

Cmd/Ctrl+B has always collapsed the sidebar, but nothing on screen said so. The
title bar now carries a sidebar button at the sidebar's own edge to close it,
and the same mark where the old menu glyph was to bring it back. Both name your
actual shortcut in their tooltip, so a remapped key still reads correctly.

### Fixed

- **The command palette scrolled the page instead of the selection.** Arrowing
  through the list moved everything behind the palette and left the highlight
  where it was. Two causes: keeping the selected row visible asked the browser
  to scroll every container up to the window rather than just the list, and
  focusing the search field made the layout underneath scroll to "reveal" it.
  Search All Notes had both faults and is fixed with it.
- **A wheel past the end of either list** no longer scrolls the page underneath.
- **Neither dialog runs off a short window any more.** They shrink to fit
  instead of leaving the last rows below the edge of the screen.

### Under the hood

The Linux release build once spent two hours stuck in a package install,
retrying a mirror that had gone dark, because nothing set a network timeout or
a job limit. Both are in place now, so a stuck build fails in minutes and can be
retried rather than holding a runner all afternoon.
